p: divided in the midst of thee: He arms the godly against the great temptations that would come, before they enjoyed this prosperous estate promised under Christ, that when these dangers came, they might know that they were warned of them before.
fought in the day of battle: As your fathers and you have had experience both at the Red Sea, and at all other times.
mount of Olives: By this manner of speech the Prophet shows God's power and care over his Church, and how he will as it were by a miracle save it.
valley: So that out of all the parts of the world, they will see Jerusalem, which was before his with this mountain: and this he means of the spiritual Jerusalem the Church.
valley of the mountains: He speaks of the hypocrites, who could not abide God's presence, but would flee into all places, where they might hide themselves among the mountains.
earthquake in the days of Uzziah: Read Am 1:1.

my God shall come: Because they did not credit the Prophet's words, he turns to God and comforts himself in that that he knew that these things would come, and says, "You, O God, with your angels will come to perform this great thing."
not day: Signifying, that there would be great troubles in the Church, and that the time of it is in the Lord's hands, yet at length (which is here meant by the evening) God would send comfort.
waters shall go out from Jerusalem: That is, the spiritual graces of God, which would always continue in most abundance.
LORD: All idolatry and superstition will be abolished, and there will be one God, one faith, and one religion.
as a plain from Geba to: This new Jerusalem will be seen through all the world, and will excel the first in excellency, wealth, and greatness.
a great tumult from the LORD: God will not only raise up war outside, but sedition at home to test them.
the hand of his neighbour: To hurt and oppress him.
gold: The enemies are rich, and therefore will not come to entreat, but to destroy and shed blood.
plague: As the men would be destroyed, Zec 14:12.
Egypt shall not go up: By the Egyptians, who were the greatest enemies to true religion, he means all the Gentiles.
bells of the horses: Signifying to whatever service they were put now (whether to labour, or to serve in war), they were now holy, because the Lord had sanctified them.
pots in the LORD'S house shall: The one as precious as the other, because they will be sanctified.
Canaanite in the house of the: But all will be pure and clean, and there will neither by hypocrites, nor any that will corrupt the true service of God.
